claude.sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

links.outcome: Model accuracy under prompt and language variation (2x2 factorial design)
links.effect: Without-prompt and language changes caused large accuracy drops for some models, e.g. English without-prompt N-staging Qwen3 36.8% vs DeepSeek-R1 79.8%; with-prompt T-staging all models >91% (Q=4.97, p=0.174) in Chinese.
links.quote: In the challenging English without-prompt N-staging scenario, DeepSeek-R1 retained an accuracy of 79.8%.

links.outcome: Accuracy differences between Chinese and English inputs across models
links.effect: Most models showed decreased accuracy moving from Chinese to English; Qwen3 English without-prompt N-staging fell to 36.8% (QWK 0.02), while DeepSeek-R1 remained stable at 79.8%.
links.quote: Regarding the impact of language, while most models showed decreased accuracy when transitioning from Chinese to English contexts, DeepSeek-R1 demonstrated cross-lingual stability.

links.outcome: LLM T/N staging accuracy versus expert consensus reference standard
links.effect: T-staging average accuracy DeepSeek-R1 91.4%, Qwen3 88.8%, GPT-4o 84.2%, Grok-3 81.3%; N-staging 84.2%, 68.4%, 65.0%, 51.9%.
links.quote: The N-staging task proved significantly more challenging than T-staging for all models.

links.outcome: Clinically consequential cross-stage misclassification errors in N-staging
links.effect: Grok-3 misclassified 30.3% of N3 cases as N1; Qwen3 classified 91.8% of N0, 89.8% of N1 and 92.7% of N3 as N2 in English without-prompt; DeepSeek-R1 errors mostly adjacent.
links.quote: Grok-3, for example, misclassified 30.3% of N3 cases as the distant N1 stage under identical conditions ( Supplementary Material , Figures S1–S4 ).

unlisted_practices: Providing explicit staging definitions in the prompt to reduce model dependence on internal knowledge

openai.sample_unit: EUS reports for T-staging; 579 for N-staging

links.effect: Overall N-staging accuracy: DeepSeek-R1 84.2%, Qwen3 68.4%, GPT-4o 65.0%, Grok-3 51.9%.
links.quote: Nevertheless, DeepSeek-R1 retained a substantial lead with an overall average accuracy of 84.2%, significantly surpassing Qwen3 (68.4%), GPT-4o (65.0%), and Grok-3 (51.9%).

links.outcome: accuracy across language and prompt scenarios
links.effect: English without-prompt N-staging: DeepSeek-R1 79.8% vs GPT-4o 60.8%, Grok-3 43.7%, Qwen3 36.8%.
links.quote: For instance, in the English without-prompt condition, DeepSeek-R1 achieved a significantly higher accuracy of 79.8%, compared to 60.8% for GPT-4o, 43.7% for Grok-3, and 36.8% for Qwen3.

links.effect: Chinese without-prompt N-staging: DeepSeek-R1 outperformed GPT-4o OR = 4.64, Qwen3 OR = 2.43, Grok-3 OR = 5.86; all p < 0.001.
links.quote: For instance, in the Chinese without-prompt N-staging condition, DeepSeek-R1′s superiority was substantial against GPT-4o (OR = 4.64, 95% CI [3.20–6.74], p < 0.001), Qwen3 (OR = 2.43, 95% CI [1.52–3.89], p < 0.001), and Grok-3 (OR = 5.86, 95% CI [4.29–8.00], p < 0.001).

links.effect: With explicit instructions, all models achieved > 90% T-staging accuracy; Chinese T all-model average was 92.8% with prompt versus 79.7% without.
links.quote: In our study, all models demonstrated high performance levels under ideal conditions with explicit instructions, achieving > 90% accuracy in T-staging tasks and indicating strong baseline capabilities.

links.outcome: T-staging accuracy and cross-model variability with versus without prompt templates
links.effect: With prompts, all models achieved >91% accuracy in Chinese T-staging with minimal variation (Q=4.97, p=0.174); without prompts, accuracy averaged 79.7% with significant heterogeneity (Q=226.77, p<0.001).
links.quote: Specifically, in the with-prompt conditions, performance variation was minimal, all models achieved accuracy exceeding 91%, with Cochran’s Q test confirming no significant difference (Q = 4.97, p = 0.174).

primary.practice: prompt engineering and cross-lingual prompt design
